medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 recommends optimal diabetes management to reduce CKD progression

medications.purpose: Renal protection and blood pressure control
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I for CKD with hypertension or proteinuria

medications.purpose: Slow CKD progression and reduce cardiovascular risk
medications.nice_justification: NG203 SGLT2 inhibitor for CKD with ACR ≥2.6 mg/mmol or eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m²

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 statin recommended for all CKD patients

medications.purpose: Treat iron‑deficiency anemia pending iron studies
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises anemia screening and iron therapy if deficiency is confirmed

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive glucose‑lowering effect increasing risk of hypoglycaemia
interactions_checked.action: Advise patient to monitor blood glucose closely for 2 weeks; consider 10‑20 % reduction in insulin dose if hypoglycaemia occurs

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined effect on volume status may cause hypotension or renal function decline
interactions_checked.action: Check orthostatic BP, serum creatinine and potassium at 1–2 weeks after initiation

interactions_checked.interaction: Opposing effects on serum potassium (ACE‑I ↑K⁺, thiazide ↓K⁺) and additive renal effects
interactions_checked.action: Monitor serum potassium and creatinine at 1–2 weeks, then at 4–6 weeks

interactions_checked.interaction: Iron can cause gastrointestinal upset that may affect insulin absorption if vomiting/diarrhoea occurs
interactions_checked.action: Take iron with food and separate from insulin injection sites; monitor Hb and GI tolerance

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention (NG203 contraindicated drugs)
contraindications.alternative: Paracetamol or topical analgesics for pain

contraindications.reason: Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury (NG203 contraindicated drugs)
contraindications.alternative: Continue ACE‑I alone; do not add ARB

assumptions_warnings: Albumin‑to‑creatinine ratio (ACR) not provided; assumed proteinuria meets the ≥2.6 mg/mmol threshold for SGLT2‑inhibitor eligibility.
Lipid profile and liver function tests not available; assumed normal and no contraindication to statin.
Serum potassium not recorded; assumed ≤5.0 mmol/L before starting dapagliflozin and chlorthalidone.
Iron studies (ferritin, transferrin‑saturation) missing; empirical oral iron started pending results.
HbA1c value of 2.8 % is implausible; repeat measurement required before further diabetes adjustments.
Pregnancy status not documented; assumed patient is not pregnant (ACE‑I and statin are teratogenic).
Allergy history not provided; will confirm no hypersensitivity to ACE‑I, statin, SGLT2‑i, or iron.
treatment_summary: The plan adds dapagliflozin, atorvastatin, oral iron and a low‑dose thiazide diuretic, while up‑titrating lisinopril to 20 mg for optimal renal protection and BP control. Existing insulin, ACE‑I and amlodipine are continued. Interactions are monitored, NSAIDs are avoided, and regular labs (eGFR, ACR, potassium, LFTs, iron studies, HbA1c) are scheduled per NICE NG203. Non‑pharmacological advice includes low‑salt diet, smoking cessation, weight management and avoidance of nephrotoxic OTC drugs.
